## The source
```c
#include <limits.h>
#ifndef __cplusplus

#endif
typedef int value_type;

/*@
  axiomatic HasEqualNeighbors
  {
    predicate
    HasEqualNeighbors{L}(value_type* a, integer n) =
      \exists integer i; 0 <= i < n-1 && a[i] == a[i+1];
  }
*/
size_type
adjacent_find(const value_type* a, size_type n)
{
  if (1u < n) {
    for (size_type i = 0u; i + 1u < n; ++i) {
      if (a[i] == a[i + 1u]) {
        //@ assert HasEqualNeighbors(a, i+2);

      }

  }
  //@ assert !HasEqualNeighbors(a, n);
}
```

## Hard constraints
- Do NOT modify any original C token or any original `//@ assert(...)`. Only ADD ACSL annotations (loop contracts, function contract).
- Never use `admit`, `assume`, `axiom`, or unproved fallbacks. All annotations must be PROVEN by Frama-C WP.

## Suggested approach (you must verify, and may strengthen/weaken as needed)
The two goals:
1. Inside loop where `a[i]==a[i+1]`, prove `//@ assert HasEqualNeighbors(a, i+2);` — witness is index i, since 0<=i<(i+2)-1 and a[i]==a[i+1].
2. After loop completes, prove `//@ assert !HasEqualNeighbors(a, n);`.

For goal 2 you need a loop invariant that carries the "no equal neighbor found so far" knowledge to the loop exit, i.e.
`loop invariant \forall integer k; 0 <= k < i ==> a[k] != a[k+1];`
combined with loop bounds `loop invariant 0 <= i <= n;`, `loop assigns i;`, and a variant (e.g. `loop variant n - i;`). At loop exit the guard `i+1u < n` is false so i >= n-1, which together with the forall-invariant proves `!\exists k; 0<=k<n-1 && a[k]==a[k+1]` i.e. `!HasEqualNeighbors(a, n)`.
